title_en: Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, Jiang Kerong, Dai Jiabao, Fang Xiaowei, Ni Xiance — smuggling, active bribery, passive bribery, and malfeasance case
keywords_en: Criminal; Smuggling; Bribery (active); Acceptance of bribe; Engagement in malpractices for personal gain; First instance; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; High People's Court; Jiangxi Province; Fujian Province; Guangdong Province; Natural person; State organ; Criminal Law; Determination of intent to smuggle; Distinction between active bribery and extortion of bribe; Characterization of engaging in malpractices for personal gain; Partial support; Smuggling of video recorders; Splitting into smaller parts and signing separate contracts; Using official authority to facilitate customs clearance; Accepting kickbacks
full_text_en:
Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, Jiang Kerong, Dai Jiabao, Fang Xiaowei, Ni Xiance — case of smuggling, bribery, acceptance of bribes, and abuse of power

Defendant: Guo Yong, male, 33 years old, former Deputy Manager of the Business Department of Jiangxi Honghai Electronics Co., Ltd. Arrested on October 23, 1986.

Defendant: Li Gongqing, male, 32 years old, former Deputy Section Chief of the Technology Import Department of Fujian Fuxing Industrial Import and Export Corporation. Arrested on October 23, 1986.

Defendant: Jiang Kerong, male, 53 years old, former General Manager of Jiangxi Honghai Electronics Co., Ltd. Arrested on October 23, 1986.

Defendant: Dai Jiabao, male, 55 years old, former Manager of Fujian Fuxing Industrial Import and Export Corporation. Arrested on October 23, 1986.

Defendant: Fang Xiaowei, male, 31 years old, former Computer Software Programmer in the Computer Science Section of the Zhuhai Economic and Technical Information Center, Guangdong Province. Arrested on October 23, 1986.

Defendant: Ni Xiance, male, 51 years old, former Governor of Jiangxi Province (removed from office by the Jiangxi Provincial People's Congress on October 23, 1986). Arrested on January 10, 1987.

The case of defendants Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, Jiang Kerong, Dai Jiabao, Fang Xiaowei, and Ni Xiance for smuggling, bribery, acceptance of bribes, and abuse of power was initiated by the Nanchang Municipal People's Procuratorate, Jiangxi Province, which filed a public prosecution with the Nanchang Intermediate People's Court. The Nanchang Intermediate People's Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and conducted a public trial, finding the following facts:

At the end of 1984, through the introduction of Fang Xiaowei, Guo Yong and Li Gongqing became acquainted and discussed matters related to the import of video recorders. On January 22, 1985, Li Gongqing, on behalf of Fujian Fuxing Industrial Import and Export Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Fuxing Company), and a certain Chen, Vice Manager of Hong Kong Jinlong Enterprise Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinlong Company), agreed to smuggle video recorders by breaking down the import into smaller units and signing separate contracts. Accordingly, two contracts were signed: one for the purchase of 2,000 sets of upper and lower covers of Japanese Aiwa brand video recorders; the other for the purchase of 2,000 sets of other parts and components of Japanese Aiwa brand video recorders. The total amount was USD 600,000, equivalent to RMB 1.68 million. On the 24th, Li Gongqing arrived in Nanchang and discussed the import of video recorders with Guo Yong. Subsequently, with the consent of Jiang Kerong, Guo Yong, on behalf of Jiangxi Honghai Electronics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Honghai Company), and Li Gongqing signed a letter of authorization, the contents of which were: Honghai Company authorized Fuxing Company to import 2,000 Japanese video recorders, with a total amount of USD 600,000; the payment for the goods was to be remitted by Honghai Company into the account of Jinlong Company; Fuxing Company was to provide customs declaration documents, and Honghai Company was to handle the customs declaration procedures; Honghai Company was to pay Fuxing Company an 8.4% service fee. On the 26th, after returning to Fuzhou, Li Gongqing drafted two reports applying for the import of 2,000 sets of video recorder parts and components, which he submitted to Dai Jiabao for review. Dai Jiabao, knowing that video recorders were a product subject to state import restrictions, and that Fuxing Company was importing complete video recorders rather than parts and components, and that splitting the approval documents and import licenses was to circumvent customs inspection, nevertheless signed and approved the receipt of the approval documents. Li Gongqing took the approval documents to the Fujian Provincial Commission of Foreign Economic Relations and Trade and obtained two import cargo licenses. Li Gongqing then arranged for someone to forward the approval documents, licenses, blank customs declaration forms, and contracts to Guo Yong. Jiang Kerong and Guo Yong, knowing that video recorders were a product subject to state import restrictions and that import required approval from the State Economic Commission, and that the approval documents provided by Li Gongqing were split and had not been approved by the State Economic Commission, and that the contract and the letter of authorization were inconsistent, nevertheless had Guo Yong proceed to make a preliminary customs declaration at Wenjindu Customs. On March 5, Honghai Company instructed the Nanchang Branch of the Bank of China to issue a letter of credit to the Hong Kong branch of the Bank of China. On April 2, Guo Yong, in Guangzhou, signed with a certain Chen, Chairman of Jinlong Company, a supplementary contract under which Jinlong Company was to provide certificates of origin and quality certificates for the complete video recorders of Japanese origin. On April 19, after receiving the relevant documents from Jinlong Company, Guo Yong added a postscript on the receipt for the documents: "Do not disassemble the machines too much; it is sufficient to remove only the upper and lower covers." On April 22 and 23, when the goods entered the country in two batches through Wenjindu, Customs discovered that they were not video recorder parts and components but complete machines, and decided to seize them. On June 7, Wenjindu Customs issued a decision notice on smuggling cases, deciding to confiscate all the goods and impose a fine of RMB 1.5 million. At this point, Guo Yong and Jiang Kerong submitted reports to Customs requesting payment of taxes and fines and release of the confiscated video recorders. After Customs refused, Jiang Kerong instructed Guo Yong to seek help from Ni Xiance through Guo Yong's sister, a certain Guo.

On June 29, 1985, a certain Guo telephoned Ni Xiance, saying: "Honghai Company's video recorders have been seized by Customs, and my brother handled this matter personally. The situation is very serious. The leaders of Honghai Company want to report to you specifically; you had better help resolve it." That afternoon, Ni Xiance listened to reports from Jiang Kerong, Guo Yong, and others regarding the confiscation of the imported video recorders by Customs, and reviewed the letter of authorization, contract, approval documents, license, and Customs' decision. Because Ni Xiance was engaged in an illicit sexual relationship with a certain Guo, and to cater to her personal feelings, although he knew that Guo Yong and others had colluded with Fuxing Company to smuggle video recorders, he used his official position and wrote personal letters to a certain Chen, Director of the Jiangxi Provincial Economic and Trade Commission's Shenzhen Transit Station, and a certain Han, Deputy Director of the Jiangxi Provincial Office for Foreign Economic and Technical Cooperation, and telephoned a certain Gu, former Director of the Jiangxi Provincial Economic and Trade Commission, and a certain Li, Director of Jiujiang Customs, falsely claiming that Honghai Company had imported video recorder parts and components, intentionally concealing and covering up the true facts of Guo Yong and others' smuggling of video recorders, and asking them to intercede with the General Administration of Customs. On September 2, Ni Xiance instructed a certain Zeng, the authorized litigation agent of Honghai Company, to telephone the General Administration of Customs in the name of the provincial governor, exerting pressure. After the General Administration of Customs made a decision upholding the disposition of Wenjindu Customs, Ni Xiance, in order to absolve Guo Yong of criminal liability, again used his official position and issued instructions to the Jiangxi Provincial Planning Commission and the Nanchang Branch of the Bank of China to resolve the foreign exchange quota for Honghai Company to pay the Hong Kong merchant. As a result of Ni Xiance's actions, the directly responsible person of this particularly large-scale smuggling case, Guo Yong, was not timely prosecuted.

During the process of entrusting the import of video recorders, Li Gongqing and Fang Xiaowei, in consultation with Guo Yong and with the consent of Jiang Kerong, agreed that Honghai Company would pay Li and Fang a "kickback" of RMB 60,000. On February 5, 1985, Guo Yong paid Fang Xiaowei RMB 30,000, of which Li Gongqing received RMB 20,000 and Fang Xiaowei received RMB 10,000.

In addition, from the end of 1984 to the beginning of 1985, during activities related to purchasing video recorders and video tapes in Guangdong, Guo Yong accepted bribes on three occasions totaling RMB 6,375. In September 1985, during the process of acting as an agent for the import of transistors by Fuzhou Baihuting Trade Company, Li Gongqing accepted a bribe of RMB 6,000.

The above facts are confirmed by the contracts for smuggling video recorders, the supplementary contract, the letter of authorization, instructions, licenses, the decision letter of Customs on handling the smuggling case, the appraisal of the state commodity inspection authority, account books and document examination reports, Ni Xiance's personal letters and instructions, and witness testimony. The facts are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, and they are sufficient to establish the findings.

The Nanchang Intermediate People's Court found in its trial that: the defendants Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, Jiang Kerong, and Dai Jiabao, with the aim of seeking profits, violated customs regulations, evaded customs supervision, seriously disrupted the state's system of foreign trade control, and jointly smuggled 2,000 video recorders, involving an especially large amount, with serious circumstances, thereby constituting the crime of smuggling as provided in Article 118 of the Criminal Law. Guo Yong, being a state functionary, took advantage of his official position to accept bribes or offer bribes to others, thereby constituting the crimes of acceptance of bribes and offering bribes as provided in Article 185, paragraphs 1 and 3 of the Criminal Law. Li Gongqing, being a state functionary, colluded with defendant Fang Xiaowei to jointly accept bribes, involving a large amount, thereby constituting the crime of acceptance of bribes as provided in Article 185, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law. Jiang Kerong, being a state functionary, offered bribes to others for the purpose of obtaining illegal profits for his unit, involving a large amount, thereby constituting the crime of offering bribes as provided in Article 185, paragraph 3 of the Criminal Law. Defendant Ni Xiance, clearly knowing the major smuggling activities of Guo Yong and others, and in order to prevent Guo Yong from being prosecuted, used his official position to deliberately conceal and cover up their criminal facts, thereby constituting the crime of abuse of power as provided in Article 188 of the Criminal Law and Item (3) of Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy. Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, and Jiang Kerong each committed multiple crimes, and in accordance with Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, they are to be subjected to concurrent punishment for multiple crimes. Given Jiang Kerong's criminal circumstances and his expression of repentance, in accordance with Article 67 of the Criminal Law, a suspended sentence may be imposed. Given that Dai Jiabao's criminal circumstances were minor, in accordance with Article 32 of the Criminal Law, he may be exempted from criminal punishment. Accordingly, on April 11, 1987, the judgment was as follows:

Defendant Guo Yong was sentenced to three years' imprisonment for the crime of smuggling, one year's imprisonment for the crime of offering bribes, and one year and six months' imprisonment for the crime of acceptance of bribes, with a combined sentence of five years' imprisonment.

Defendant Li Gongqing was sentenced to three years' imprisonment for the crime of smuggling and eight years' imprisonment for the crime of acceptance of bribes, with a combined sentence of ten years' imprisonment.

Defendant Jiang Kerong was sentenced to two years' imprisonment for the crime of smuggling and one year's imprisonment for the crime of offering bribes, with a combined sentence of two years and six months' imprisonment, suspended for three years.

Defendant Dai Jiabao was exempted from criminal punishment for the crime of smuggling.

Defendant Fang Xiaowei was sentenced to three years' imprisonment for the crime of acceptance of bribes.

Defendant Ni Xiance was sentenced to two years' imprisonment for the crime of abuse of power.

All unlawful gains of defendants Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, and Fang Xiaowei were to be recovered in accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law.

After the first-instance judgment, Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, Jiang Kerong, Dai Jiabao, Fang Xiaowei, and Ni Xiance all refused to accept the judgment and appealed separately to the Jiangxi High People's Court. Guo Yong's grounds for appeal were that he had no intention or act of smuggling; that Li Gongqing's demand for a bribe from him was not an act of offering a bribe; and that although he had committed the crime of acceptance of bribes, this constituted voluntary surrender and he had returned the illicit gains. Li Gongqing's grounds for appeal were that he did not violate the state's system of foreign trade control or evade customs supervision; that he did not demand a "kickback" from Guo Yong; that after Customs seized the goods, he voluntarily returned the money, which constituted discontinuation of the crime; and that the bribe he accepted from Baihuting Trade Company was RMB 3,500, not RMB 6,000. Jiang Kerong's grounds for appeal were that agreeing to entrust the import of video recorders was part of his duties as General Manager, and that agreeing to pay Li Gongqing RMB 30,000 was for business entertainment expenses, not a bribe. Dai Jiabao's grounds for appeal were that there was no fact of joint smuggling with Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, and Jiang Kerong. Fang Xiaowei's ground for appeal was that he did not take advantage of his official position and did not jointly demand a "kickback" with Li Gongqing. Ni Xiance's grounds for appeal were that he did not clearly know the true circumstances of Guo Yong and others' smuggling crimes and had no intention or acts to conceal or cover up Guo Yong's crimes or to bend the law.

The Jiangxi High People's Court conducted a public trial of the case from May 27 to 30, 1987, and found that: Guo Yong, Deputy Manager of the Business Department of Honghai Company, and Li Gongqing, Deputy Section Chief of the Technology Import Department of Fuxing Company, in the joint crime, bore direct responsibility for the specific implementation of evading the state's approval requirements for importing video recorders, evading customs supervision and import duties in the smuggling act; Jiang Kerong, General Manager of Honghai Company, and Dai Jiabao, Manager of Fuxing Company, bore supervisory responsibility for the smuggling of video recorders. The above four appellants' grounds for appeal denying the crime of smuggling were not established. The grounds for appeal of Jiang Kerong and Guo Yong, that using RMB 30,000 of public funds to bribe Li Gongqing and Fang Xiaowei for the purpose of seeking exorbitant profits for their company, were not established due to reliable and sufficient evidence. The evidence that Guo Yong used his official position to accept a bribe of RMB 6,000 was reliable and sufficient and could not be denied. The fact that Guo Yong, after the case was discovered and during interrogation, confessed to the facts of accepting bribes and returned all the illicit gains did not constitute voluntary surrender. Although the court of first instance imposed a lenient punishment on Guo Yong for the crime of acceptance of bribes, considering his attitude of admission and return of illicit gains, a further lenient punishment could be given as appropriate. Li Gongqing, using his work position, colluded with Fang Xiaowei to jointly accept a bribe of RMB 30,000, with Li receiving RMB 20,000; the act of accepting bribes had been completed and the harmful consequences had already occurred, which did not constitute discontinuation of the crime. Li Gongqing voluntarily returned the illicit gains after Customs seized the smuggled goods. Although the first-instance judgment had already considered this circumstance, a lenient punishment could still be given. The bribe of RMB 6,000 that Li Gongqing accepted from Baihuting Trade Company was confirmed by the testimony of the bribe-giver; the facts were clear and the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and the ground of appeal was inconsistent with the facts and was not accepted. Fang Xiaowei's acceptance of bribes was a joint crime with Li Gongqing, and he was an accomplice in Li Gongqing's crime of acceptance of bribes; the ground of appeal denying acceptance of bribes was not established. Although the first-instance judgment gave Fang Xiaowei a lenient punishment, considering that he first confessed to the joint bribery of RMB 30,000 and returned all illicit gains, a further lenient punishment could be given. Ni Xiance, being a state functionary, in order to cater to the personal feelings of a certain Guo, clearly knowing that Guo Yong and others were smuggling video recorders, used his official position to deliberately conceal and cover up the criminal facts of Guo Yong and others, instructed others to intercede with Customs and exert pressure; in order to prevent the smuggling crimes of Guo Yong and others from being exposed, after the General Administration of Customs made a decision upholding the disposition of Wenjindu Customs, he again directed the relevant departments to resolve the foreign exchange quota for Honghai Company to pay the Hong Kong merchant. Ni Xiance's grounds of appeal were not established.

The Jiangxi High People's Court confirmed that the facts of the first-instance judgment were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the conviction was accurate, and the trial procedure was lawful. After deliberation by the collegial panel and decision by the Adjudication Committee, in accordance with Items (1) and (2) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on May 30, 1987, the judgment was as follows:

1. The portions of the first-instance judgment of the Nanchang Intermediate People's Court concerning the convictions of Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, Jiang Kerong, and Dai Jiabao for the crime of smuggling, Guo Yong and Jiang Kerong for the crime of offering bribes, and Ni Xiance for the crime of abuse of power are affirmed.

2. The portions of the first-instance judgment concerning the sentences for Guo Yong, Li Gongqing, and Fang Xiaowei for the crime of acceptance of bribes are reversed.

3. Guo Yong's sentence for the crime of acceptance of bribes is changed to one year's imprisonment, and combined with his sentences for the crimes of offering bribes and smuggling, the executed sentence is fixed at four years and six months' imprisonment. Li Gongqing's sentence for the crime of acceptance of bribes is changed to six years' imprisonment, and combined with his sentence for the crime of smuggling, the executed sentence is fixed at eight years' imprisonment. Fang Xiaowei's sentence for the crime of acceptance of bribes is changed to two years' imprisonment.
